title: Production AI and Engineering Team Design: InfoQ’s November Certification Cohorts
gist: InfoQ announced three November 2026 online certification cohorts (two AI Engineering, one High-Performing Teams); the promo embeds a thesis that AI code speed does not shorten delivery time because review, approvals and rework become the bottleneck.

insights.claim: Faster code production does not necessarily shorten delivery time, because review, approvals, infrastructure dependencies or rework may become the limiting step.
insights.speaker: InfoQ
insights.so_what: Productivity gains from AI coding tools may be capped by downstream process constraints, tempering ROI claims.
insights.quote: Increasing the speed of code production does not necessarily shorten delivery time.
insights.locator: Team Design When AI Changes the Flow of Work

insights.claim: Introducing AI agents changes who prepares context, reviews output and remains accountable for decisions, so team operating models need to be redesigned around these roles and around whether familiar output metrics remain informative.
insights.speaker: InfoQ
insights.so_what: Organizational redesign and measurement, not tooling alone, is positioned as the next enterprise AI services need.
insights.locator: Introducing AI agents also changes who prepares context

insights.claim: Production AI work involves more than model selection: retrieval can produce stale or incomplete context, autonomous agents require decisions on control and verification, and shared AI infrastructure raises questions of ownership and inference costs.
insights.speaker: InfoQ
insights.so_what: Value in enterprise AI is shifting to retrieval quality, evaluation and infrastructure governance.
insights.locator: AI applications involve more than model selection

insights.claim: The AI Engineering curriculum compares vector retrieval with Graph RAG, evaluates single-agent versus multi-agent designs, and covers orchestration, inference gateways and rollout-readiness evaluations.
insights.speaker: InfoQ
insights.so_what: Indicates which topics practitioners currently treat as open design questions in agentic systems.
insights.locator: Adi Polak, author of Scaling Machine Learning with Spark

insights.claim: Lan Chu's QCon London case study described a RAG system built on more than 10,000 documents and used by more than 300 people.
insights.speaker: InfoQ
insights.so_what: Gives a sense of typical enterprise RAG scale at the practitioner level.

insights.claim: InfoQ will run three online cohorts in November 2026: AI Engineering with Adi Polak on November 12, AI Engineering with Lan Chu on November 13, and High-Performing Teams with Olimpiu Pop on November 17, each with four live hours per week plus up to two hours of independent work.
insights.speaker: InfoQ
insights.so_what: Shows media companies extending into paid cohort education tied to conference content.
insights.locator: InfoQ has published details of three online certification cohorts
